minutes.headline: Water commissioners voted the FY2023 budget and added three articles, including a PFAS pilot study, to the annual meeting warrant.
minutes.summary: The commission approved prior minutes and voted on the 2022-2023 maintenance and operating budget after a walkthrough of changes to legal counsel, debt and chemicals. It then voted to add articles six, seven and eight (a truck, SCADA/server upgrade, and a PFAS pilot study) to the annual meeting warrant. It also heard a quote for a cloud-based meter reading system and agreed to add an old business agenda section.

what_happened.line: The water commissioners voted to add articles six, seven and eight to the annual meeting warrant: a truck, a SCADA/server upgrade and a PFAS pilot study.
The commission voted on the 2022-2023 maintenance and operating budget; the minutes record the vote outcome as not audible.
The budget walkthrough covered a lower legal counsel line, rising debt payments and higher chemicals offset by lower administration, leaving no overall change.
The PFAS pilot study article was left with a blank amount pending consultant input, and grant funding for design and engineering was mentioned.
The commission heard a cloud-based meter reading quote and kept the meter upgrade on a new old business agenda section for likely consideration next fiscal year.

why_it_matters: The budget and the three warrant articles are what water district voters will be asked to approve at the annual meeting, and they bear on water rates and district spending.
The PFAS article has no amount yet, so residents will see a dollar figure only once consultant input comes in or it is set at the meeting.
watch_next: The printed annual meeting warrant, to see the amount, if any, placed on the PFAS pilot study article.
Whether the meter reading upgrade returns under old business in the next fiscal year.
